_meta: Nine students and three quiz items. Each student has a total score (their performance on the rest of the quiz, a proxy for ability) and a pass/fail (1/0) on each item. An item's job is to SEPARATE students who know the material from those who don't. Difficulty is the pass rate (fraction who got it right) — 0.5 is often called ideal. Discrimination is whether the strong students pass it more than the weak ones: split students into the top third and bottom third by total score, and take pass_rate(top) - pass_rate(bottom). A good item has high discrimination; an item everyone passes, or one the top and bottom pass equally, has zero discrimination and measures nothing — even if its difficulty looks perfect. Item A discriminates; item B is too easy; item C sits at ideal difficulty but does not discriminate at all.
